arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Boies argued the district court found Rule 23(a) requirements met. He stated the plaintiff fulfilled all certification requirements.
Mr. Sterling argued individual reliance issues predominate. He cited Basic to support this view.
Justice Ginsburg asked how the class would prove loss causation. She noted this issue usually arises at trial.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests when courts must resolve reliance and price impact. the side that brought the case wants class certification. the opposing side wants to defeat it early.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the court to certify the class. It argues reliance is presumed for all members.
the opposing side wants the court to deny certification. It argues individual reliance issues predominate.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the Basic presumption applies at certification. It claims loss causation belongs at trial.
the opposing side argues individual reliance issues predominate. It claims price impact must be resolved first.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Alito asked if the Basic presumption can be rebutted at certification.
Justice Kagan asked if materiality can be rebutted at certification. She also asked why price impact differs from other disputes.
